F3.mechanism: TWO independent faults compose. (i) nounPhraseHead() returns the trailing past participle "issued" because a participle is a content word and nothing marks it as a post-modifier. F4.responsibleFunction: semantic-evidence-binding.ts::checkStateSupported(), CORRECTED rule with requireAssertion:true, consuming predicate-role.ts::asserts()
F4.mechanism: L3-2e correctly required that a CORRECTED claim be ASSERTED rather than merely mentioned, and implemented "asserted" as role === ASSERTED_PREDICATE. That equates assertion with VERBHOOD. "drew a replacement" asserts a completed correction with a correction NOUN as the object of an action verb; tokenRole returns NP_HEAD and the claim is refused.
F4.semanticExpectation: a correction noun that is the object of a completed action verb, not under a negation, supports CORRECTED
F4.blueprintInvariant: blueprint 35.5 DISC-07; L3-INV-08 (model output is a proposal -- this vocabulary ADMITS, so it may be permissive, per the 35.1 asymmetry)
F4.defectClass: DISTINCT MECHANISM, SAME FAMILY. F1/F2/F3 are all "membership or containment standing in for a structural property". F4 is the opposite error: a STRUCTURAL test (role) applied too narrowly, refusing a construction it was never meant to exclude. It is a regression introduced by L3-2e, not a surviving lexical gate.
F4.direction: ADMISSION -- refuses a state the model correctly claimed
F4.governingAsymmetry: blueprint 35.1 -- a vocabulary used to ADMIT may be permissive. The negation guard and the mention/effective distinction must both survive.

summary.sharedMechanism: F1, F2 and F3 are ONE mechanism in three functions: a bounded structural property of a clause or noun phrase (does this segment carry a predicate? does this word close a noun phrase? is this token that token?) decided by consulting a hand-maintained lexical set or by substring containment. F4 is the mirror image and is a L3-2e regression.
